market_holds: Spot $10.68 at the 2026-11-18 seal, 5-day run-up -2.3%, 20-day +1.1%, 10.6% below the 52-week high, 20-day realised vol 19.9%, about 77k shares a day (sealed baseline). The option chain is unusable (no two-sided ATM quotes), so there is no implied move. The usual move is a 1.93% median close-to-close reaction over 6 prints. Measured to the OPEN, which is what this window scores, the last 7 prints gapped -1.75, -3.90, +0.09, -1.16, +3.94, -8.77 and -4.23% (Yahoo daily bars, own arithmetic): median absolute gap 3.9%, 5 of 7 negative, and the two big gap-downs (Apr and Jul 2026) both closed the day higher. There is effectively no consensus. Nasdaq/Zacks has no forecast, the AP/Zacks snapshot of the Q3 print quoted no estimate, and aggregators show one stale Hold. The company gives no numeric guide. Its 10-Q gives a schedule instead: the remaining $11.7M of Phase 2D lot revenue and $0.8M of Phase 2C revenue were to be recognised by fiscal year-end on 2026-08-31. Positioning: Maran Capital owns 14.7% and has nominated five directors for the 2027 annual meeting; put/call open interest is 1.3 on only 239 contracts.
view: Q4 FY26 (June to August) should be the company's largest quarter, if Phase 2D was delivered on schedule. The Q3 10-Q says $11.7M of Phase 2D lot revenue plus $0.8M of Phase 2C revenue remained to be recognised by fiscal year-end. Q4 FY25 had $7.7M of lot sales, and EPS that quarter was $0.25. Oil and gas water sales were running at $2.0M a quarter of commercial water revenue in Q3, and the company expected that demand to continue. My own rebuild puts Q4 pre-tax income near $9-11M and Q4 EPS near $0.25-0.35, so FY26 EPS would be about $0.60-0.70 against $0.54. The headline would likely be record yearly net income, up 15-30%. Because no analyst estimate is published, a naive reader extrapolating $0.12 a quarter would see a large beat. Against that: (1) the schedule was public in the 10-Q and the holder base is concentrated and sophisticated. The direct analog, last year's equally foreseeable big Q4 (Phase 2C), opened -1.2% and closed -1.6%. (2) Phase 2D has already slipped once: in April the company said it would finish in fiscal Q3, in July it was 84% done and the date moved to year-end. Another slip would push revenue into FY27 Q1 and leave Q4 well short of the schedule. (3) The 8:30 ET call before the open will be about FY27, and FY27 looks weak. The 159 Phase 2E lots were being built without a signed builder contract as of July. Lennar's share of revenue fell from 21% to 5% and KB Home's from 20% to 4%. The rental build-out is paused. (4) This thin stock's opening print has gapped down on 5 of 7 recent prints and then recovered intraday. The activist fight adds an upside tail: management may pair the print with a capital-return announcement, since only 85,974 shares remain under the buyback authorisation. Net, a strong reported number is likely, but I cannot show that the price does not already hold it, and the scored print is a noisy, negatively skewed opening cross. I land near 50 with a slight lean down.

recommendation.reason: The likely strong Q4 follows mechanically from revenue the company scheduled in its own 10-Q. I cannot show the price is behind it, and last year's equally foreseeable big Q4 opened lower. The opening cross on this stock has a negative, noisy tendency, and FY27 lot contracting is unresolved. Neither side reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A release showing Phase 2D fully recognised (Q4 EPS of $0.30 or more, FY up 25% or more) together with signed Phase 2E builder contracts or a new buyback or capital-return programme would make a positive open likely. A Phase 2D slip into FY27 would make it clearly negative.

self_critique: The strongest case for a long: with no published estimate, a record yearly headline (EPS up 15-30%) on an uncovered stock read by retail and by screens could gap it up 3-5%, as the January 2026 print did (+3.9% gap). The board is in a proxy fight and has every reason to dress the release with capital returns. The case against the slight down lean is that last year's single analog is one data point and that open-gap statistics over 7 prints are noise. Both points only push toward 50, which is where I am.
approach_notes: Rebuilding the quarter from the 10-Q's disclosed remaining-revenue schedule (P3 own arithmetic) was the most useful step. Measuring past reactions to the open rather than the close (P6, window) changed the size estimate a lot. P4's 'priced in is a claim to prove' cut both ways here: with no consensus I could show neither priced nor unpriced, so the playbook gives no route for uncovered names whose surprise is mechanically foreseeable from the filings.
